exposure: Sequential isosorbide mononitrate (IMN) followed by misoprostol for labour induction
outcome: Maternal adverse effects (hypotension, headache, uterine hyperstimulation)
Neonatal parameters (Apgar scores, NICU admissions, birth weights)
cohort: The study included 200 term pregnant women with a Bishop score <6 who were undergoing labour induction.
finding: Sequential IMN and misoprostol effectively shorten labour duration and reduce misoprostol requirement but are associated with increased maternal side effects, without compromising fetal safety.
mod_finding: A higher percentage of women in the sequential IMN and misoprostol group achieved vaginal delivery (81% vs 69%), though this difference was not statistically significant.
birth_weight: Birth weights were comparable between the groups as a neonatal outcome.
